result:
The mindmap work is verified: the new and existing mindmap tests, the tenant-scope lint test, `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` all pass, and no new mypy errors come from my code. The one thing I couldn't do is the `git stash` baseline comparison, which was denied. For the suite-wide failures I'm relying on inspection.

## Changes this round
- **Fix 1 (`mindmap_resolve.py`):** the checks now run in the order you suggested.
  - (a) A read `tenant_tx` runs team → map → live → member → not root → open.
  - (b) If a resolver is given, the self-check runs, then the `system_tx` access check.
  - (c) The write `tenant_tx` re-runs the same checks, then `settle_member`, `insert_reference` and `log_event`.
  - A stray resolver id can no longer mask a map or node error.
- **Fix 2:** I removed the unused `MapNodeNotFoundError` from `service.py`.
- **New test:** `test_other_map_node_with_valid_resolver_reports_node_error` checks that another map's node plus a valid resolver gives -32602 with path `node_id`, and that no node status or edge changes.
- **Test bug found and fixed:** the inaccessible-resolver test inserted a memory with `visibility='private'`, which violates `memories_visibility_check`. It now uses `'team'`.
- **Typing and format cleanup:** the new test file's helpers are typed, and `ruff format` reformatted `mindmap_get.py` and the new test file.

## Commands

| Command | Status | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `alembic upgrade head` | ran | no output |
| `alembic current` | ran | `0044_mindmap_branch_status (head)` |
| `pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_mindmap_resolve_models.py` | ran | 15 passed |
| `pytest … test_mindmap_resolve_e2e.py test_mindmap_e2e.py` (first run) | ran | 18 passed, 1 failed (the `'private'` test bug above) |
| same, after the fix | ran | 19 passed |
| same four mindmap files plus `tests/unit/test_lint_tenant_scope.py`, after final formatting | ran | 48 passed |
| `pytest … tests/unit tests/integration` | ran | 37 failed, 1221 passed, 2 skipped, 15 errors |
| full `pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --tb=no` | ran | 38 failed, 1266 passed, 31 skipped, 15 errors |
| `ruff check src tests` | ran | all checks passed |
| `ruff format --check src tests` | ran (after formatting 2 files) | 313 files already formatted |
| `mypy` | ran | 39 errors in 5 files, none from code I added |
| `git stash -u` baseline comparison | denied | not done |
| `alembic downgrade -1`, then `upgrade head` | not run | the order-3 list had no downgrade step |

The first `alembic upgrade head` of this round produced no output, so the "ran" is backed only by `alembic current` showing 0044 at head. I did not exercise `downgrade()`.

## Failures and whether they are new
- **No failure touches mindmap code.** Only three test files reference mindmap or `memory_map`, and all of them pass: `tests/integration/test_mindmap_e2e.py`, `tests/integration/test_mindmap_resolve_e2e.py` and `tests/unit/test_mindmap_resolve_models.py`.
- **Failures and errors in `tests/unit` and `tests/integration`** are all teams, enterprise, RBAC, roles-catalog and slug-schema tests, hitting fixture collisions. Examples are hard-coded `user1@example.com` (`tenants_email_key`) and `teams_created_by_tenant_id_fkey` on teardown. By inspection they are pre-existing, but I could not prove it with a stash run.
- **`tests/security/test_scope_enforcement.py::TestStatsToolScopes::test_stats_tool_requires_read_scope`** is the 38th failure. It is not caused by this change: it registers only `MemoryStatsTool` in its own `ToolRegistry` and dispatches `"memory.stats"`, which returns -32601 "method not found" (the test expects -32000). Nothing I changed touches that tool or the registry code.
- **No registry or description-completeness test failed.** `tests/unit/test_lint_tenant_scope.py` is green.

## mypy detail
- **`src` errors in files I touched:** `service.py:65` and `:76` (`resolve_map_root` and `find_live_map_seeded_from` returning `Any`) are in functions I did not change. `_mindmap_common.py:36` is likewise untouched.
- **Test-file errors:** the rest are in existing test files. `tests/integration/test_mindmap_e2e.py` has the same `BaseModel` attribute-access noise as before.
- **My new test file:** no mypy errors remain in it.

## Still open
- To close the baseline question, run `! git stash -u && pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --tb=no -rfE; git stash pop` yourself, or approve the stash.
- Run the migration round-trip (`alembic downgrade -1`, then `alembic upgrade head`) to exercise `downgrade()`.
